result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers say no and correctly trace the actual tab order (email → password → postcode → street → town), showing that the tabindex values don't match the screen. B states more clearly that positive tabindex puts these fields ahead of the header and nav, and its corrected markup keeps the same look. A's suggestion to use tabindex="-1" where needed is misleading, because -1 removes a field from the tab order, and its closing advice contradicts itself. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers say no, explain why positive tabindex is fragile and pulls fields ahead of the rest of the page, notice that password tabs second, and recommend fixing the DOM order with no tabindex. A says this more clearly, for example noting that focus jumps ahead of the header and nav. B's advice to use tabindex="-1" 'where needed' is misleading because that takes elements out of the tab order, and its WCAG aside adds length without adding much.
